title: Proactive noise mitigation and runbook autonomy for multi-region failover
creator: Noah Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pages (false-positive and low-actionability alerts) while preserving or improving sensitivity to customer-visible SLO breaches across multi-region deployments. Deliver a runbook-autopilot capability that can perform deterministic triage actions (synthetic probes, circuit-breaker toggles, traffic reroute, autoscaling commands) and either resolve or escalate incidents with audit logs and rollback safeguards.

Scope:
- Alert tuning: hysteresis windows, confidence scoring, and dynamic dampening per alert class.
- On-call runbooks: codified, machine-executable playbooks with mandatory human checkpoints for high-risk changes.
- Incident automation: safe autopilot for common degradations (hot partitions, KV cache thrash, queue backlog), including multi-region failover orchestrations and circuit-breaker soft-open behavior.
- Load shedding policy integration: automatic per-region shedding ceilings tied to SLO risk models.

Targets & Success Metrics:
- Reduce P1 noisy pages by 60% in 30 days (measured as unique pages per weekday per oncall).
- Keep customer-visible SLO breach miss rate < 0.5% after tuning.
- Mean time to first meaningful action (auto-triage or human ack) < 3 minutes for automated paths.

Design notes & approach:
1) Multi-signal confidence: combine SLO-derived signals (error budget burn rate, user-facing latency percentiles), infra signals (GPU utilization, queue depth), and synthetics (canary latencies) into a per-alert confidence score. Alerts below confidence threshold will be grouped and batched to avoid paging; they still create tickets on dashboards.
2) Hysteresis & dampening: implement configurable hysteresis windows per alert template (example: require 3 consecutive 1m breaches over 5 minutes for CPU pressure alerts) and exponential dampening for flapping signals.
3) Circuit breaker policy: introduce a soft-open state where automated remediation actions are executed (e.g., evict cold replicas, scale up pool) and only promote to full-open (traffic reroute to failover region) if confidence remains high after autoscaling attempts and synthetics fail. Soft-open has human-confirm checkpoint for high-customer-impact services.
4) Runbook Autopilot Engine: a small orchestrator that executes sequenced playbook steps: gather diagnostics, run synthetics, attempt remediation (scale/circuit toggle), evaluate heuristics, and either resolve or escalate. All actions record telemetry and produce a human-readable summary in the page. Playbooks are idempotent and support dry-run.
5) Load-shedding integration: when regional capacity drops below a safe threshold, the system computes per-route shedding priorities (based on customer tier, endpoint significance, and SLO impact) and applies progressive shedding rules. Shedding actions are reversible and logged to audit.
6) Safety & Observability: all autopilot actions require signed runbook versions, role-based authorization, and a forced human confirmation for actions that will route traffic cross-region or invalidate caches. Post-action checks run automated smoke tests and a rollback timer that will revert changes if errors increase.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive auto-remediation reduces MTTR but risks cascading changes; mitigated via soft-open, dry-run, and human checkpoints for risky actions.
- Increasing hysteresis reduces noise but can increase reaction time for true incidents; offset by multi-signal scoring and synthetics to keep high-signal events fast.

Next milestones (this cycle):
- 2026-02-25: Prototype autopilot engine in staged environment (done).
- 2026-03-02: Runbook spec review & initial playbooks for: hot-GPU pool, KV cache thrash, request queue backlog (in review).
- 2026-03-09: Canary autopilot on non-critical service (select internal team) and measure page reductions.
- 2026-03-16: Expand to public-facing model endpoints with human-confirm on cross-region reroute.

Risks:
- False positives from synthetics that don't match production traffic patterns (mitigate with traffic-shaped canaries).
- Insufficient RBAC/audit could lead to unauthorized autopilot actions (mitigate with signed playbooks + KMS-backed approvals).

Longer-term: integrate ML-based historical noise classifier, add per-customer noise profiles, and expose a tuning UI in the Console to let SREs adjust hysteresis/confidence thresholds per service.
